names.note: Read out of the list of the thirteen Syrian fathers in doxologia.ro's life of John of Zedazeni, linked from its calendar line for 7 mai, «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Zedazneli, dimpreună cu 12 ucenici din Georgia».
Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 29 noiembrie, «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Aviv, Episcop de Nekresi, Georgia», with the rank words and the see left off.
Read out of saint.gr's page for 7 Μαΐου, which heads him «Οσιος Αβιβος Μαθητης Του Οσιου Ιωαννη», with the rank words and the clause about his teacher left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's naming clause in the entry headed „Преподобни оци грузијски.“ for 7. мај ст. ст. — „А имена су њихова: Авид, Антоније, Давид, Зинон, Тадеј, Иса, Издериос, Јосиф, Михаил, Пир, Стефан и Шијо.“ The list carries no rank word and no epithet on any of the twelve; Преподобни heads the whole company in the heading and belongs to no one name, and the see or monastery each folder's English name keeps is nowhere on this page. So the bare forename is the whole of the form. **A new two-folder fold**: `abda-bishop-of-persia` holds the identical spelling as its Russian form, so this is a Serbian form meeting a Russian one, as «Капитон» and «Никон» did; the gate had no row for it before this batch. Measured before drafting.

days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 21 heads him «Священномученик Авив Некресский, Кахетинский»; with the rank off it the form is «Авив Некресский», and the second by-name, of Kakheti, is left out as the day line leaves it out. The day line gives «Сщмч. Авива , еп. Некресского».

feast.note: The calendar marks the line «(Груз.)», a commemoration of the Georgian church, and his name page 21 gives this one day. It is the same 29 ноября doxologia.ro keeps him on as a second Romanian day, which this folder's Romanian row already notes, and which that page says is the day of his martyrdom.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 29 ноября ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Авива , еп. Некресского (ок. 552-560) (Груз.).»

feast.note: doxologia.ro keeps him on a second Romanian day: its calendar for 29 noiembrie prints «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Aviv, Episcop de Nekresi, Georgia», and the life under that line says «Biserica din Georgia l-a așezat curând în ceata Sfinților și a hotărât prăznuirea pomenirii sale la 29 noiembrie, ziua muceniciei sale.» The corpus keeps one feast to a church, so 7 mai, the day of the thirteen Syrian fathers under which he was first read, stands as the feast, and 29 noiembrie is noted here.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 7 mai — «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Zedazneli, dimpreună cu 12 ucenici din Georgia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης και οι μαθητές αυτού»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps the company, and it is plainly the same company: John out of Syria and the twelve chosen to go into Iberia, whose names the page prints as «Σίω, Δαβίδ, Αντώνιος, Θαδδαίος, Στέφανος, Ισήδωρος, Μιχαήλ, Πύρρος, Ζήνων, Ισέ, Ιωσήφ και Άβιβος». **Thirteen head lines, thirteen names, so thirteen folders**, and the corpus already holds every one of them, so the whole company is upgrades and no folder is created. **`shio-of-mgvime` is the one exception and is not touched**: its `greek` row is already `venerated`, on 4 Φεβρουαρίου, so a reader may not move it; that he is listed here too is a second Greek day and is left in the report. **The Greek adds the whole story of the mission and no years at all**: the flight deeper into the desert when the crowds broke his stillness, the Theotokos appearing in a dream and commanding him to choose twelve and go to Iberia, the names written on separate papers and laid on the holy table, the night of prayer, the twelve papers an angel took from the altar into his hands before them all, the monk Euthymius left as abbot of the skete, the angel warning Bishop Eulogius of the Georgian capital of their coming, the bishop going out with clergy and people to meet them, the wonder like Pentecost by which John spoke Georgian, and their preaching through all Georgia and their veneration of the blessed places Saint Nina had passed, whom the page sends to 14 Ιανουαρίου. **No year, no hymn**, and the page does not say where any of the twelve settled afterwards — the sees and monasteries in their corpus names come from the Romanian side and nothing here is added to them. His head line is «Οσιος Αβιβος Μαθητης Του Οσιου Ιωαννη», with no epithet; but the page's own gallery of pictures captions one of them «Άγιος Άβιβος επίσκοπος Γεωργίας, Ιερομάρτυρας», Abibus bishop of Georgia, hieromartyr, which agrees with the folder's `hieromartyr` and `bishop`. It is a caption and not a statement in the notice, so `types` is not touched and the caption is recorded here. The page does not name Nekresi.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.05.2026 (7. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни оци грузијски.“

attestations.note: **The heading names nobody and the body enumerates the whole company, so the citation above is the heading whole** — „Преподобни оци грузијски.“ — per BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §4's synaxis ruling and the coordinator's first ruling for an enumerated company, and the Serbian name form is read out of the body's naming clause: „А имена су њихова: Авид, Антоније, Давид, Зинон, Тадеј, Иса, Издериос, Јосиф, Михаил, Пир, Стефан и Шијо.“ — twelve bare forenames, no rank word on any of them and no epithet, with Началник свих ових ... био је свети Јован Зедазнијски standing before the list for their leader. **The identification is the set and not the name**: the corpus already keeps these thirteen men together on this very menologion day, out of doxologia's «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Zedazneli, dimpreună cu 12 ucenici din Georgia» and saint.gr's «Όσιος Ιωάννης και οι μαθητές αυτού», and the Prologue's twelve names map one-to-one onto the twelve folders, eleven of them unmistakably — Антоније, Давид, Зинон, Тадеј, Јосиф, Михаил, Пир, Стефан, Шијо, Иса for Ise of Tsilkani and Издериос for Isidore of Samtavisi — which forces the twelfth, Авид for Abibus of Nekresi, because it is the only slot and the only name left. **`types` was deliberately not touched on any of the thirteen.** Преподобни in that heading heads a company of thirteen whose own folders carry ranks three other calendars gave them — `hieromartyr` and `bishop` for Abibus, `hierarch` and `bishop` for Jesse, `stylite` for Anthony — and a rank word covering a whole company is not evidence about one man's own grade; adding it could make `honorific.js` compose a different word to every reader, which is the `boris-michael-of-bulgaria` ruling. **No `locations` were taken**: Georgia is a country. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. **A FIRST DATE**: this folder held no `dates` at all, and the entry's „У VI веку“ gives it a `floruit` of 501–600, the same interval `anthony-of-martkopi` already holds from doxologia's identical statement.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru closes his line with an interval where it would otherwise print a year — «Сщмч. Авива , еп. Некресского (ок. 552-560) (Груз.).», about 552 to 560 — which is the narrowest dating any calendar read gives him and falls inside the sixth century the Охридски пролог puts him in: „У VI веку“. The interval is the whole of what the calendar prints and no year inside it is chosen.
